subject: 🏃 Sunday — 12 mi Long Run w/ MP Finish (Wk 5)
html:
Tomorrow: 12 mi on Bayfront flat — first 10 mi @ 8:30–9:00 (HR cap 155), then last 2 mi @ MP 7:35–7:45 (HR 150–160). Pre-run activation: hip CARs, banded lateral walks, glute bridges, plus PT-prescribed quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side). Confirm "Polar H10 — Connected" in Watch Settings before you start — do not repeat the May 24 blind run.

Gut training rehearsal #1 — target ~65 g/hr. Pre-run (5:30 AM): banana + Maurten Drink Mix 160 (40g carbs). During: Gel 160 at mile 3, Gel 100 at mile 6, Gel 100 at mile 9 (90g total, ~51 g/hr — a deliberate step up from the 48 g/hr ceiling at B2B). If the gut handles three gels clean, add a fourth Gel 100 around mile 10.5 before the MP push to nudge toward 65 g/hr. Note any GI — this data calibrates the next 7 weeks of fueling.

Gates for the fast finish: only run the MP segment if knee is 1/5 AND the fuel is sitting well. Knee 2/5 → run all 12 easy. You hit 2/5 on stairs after Wednesday's heavy strength in Boston — first non-1 of the entire V6 build — but yesterday's shakeout came back 1/5 with knee "felt good," so three rest days cleared it. The fast finish was added because you're unusually fresh after two unplanned rest days (Thu–Fri skipped in Boston) — this is where that freshness gets used to recapture the week's lost threshold dose.

Focus cue: HR discipline on the first 10 miles. You ran 8:03 on the May 24 long run when 8:45–9:15 was the prescription — that's the pattern to break. Lock the watch to HR, cap at 155, and let pace float. The MP finish is where you push; the first 10 are aerobic investment.

Week 5 of 12, Phase 2 (Strength & Threshold) — 49 days to the SF Marathon. This is the Phase 2 volume kickoff and your longest run since B2B. Every V6 session has been knee 1/5 except that single 2/5 on stairs — you're building on a clean foundation. Tonight: charge the watch, set the H10 strap next to it, prep 3–4 Maurten gels and the Drink Mix, hydrate well, bed by 10.
